note: The codex: lore entries the hero unlocks as he discovers them. $ do discover("id") unlocks one; an entry with original or person is unlocked by learning of that original or meeting that person. category must be in categories. text is plain paragraphs separated by blank lines (or a list of paragraphs). quick: true means a quick start that skips its book already knows it. hidden: true keeps a locked entry from showing even as an undiscovered row. Book sessions add entries as the story invents lore; the originals the hero has learned of also appear on their own from content/originals.json. The et_ entries are for the developer sample chapter.

collesanto.title: Collesanto
collesanto.text:
A village on a hill in the middle of Italy, three days' ride from Rome on a good road. The name means holy hill, though no one in the village can say what made it holy.

It grows wheat, barley, figs and a thin red wine. Its people are farmers and shepherds who keep to themselves, pay what the tax collectors ask and say little to strangers. At the top of the hill stands an old villa with its shutters closed, which the village avoids and does not discuss.

the_villa.title: The villa above Collesanto
the_villa.text:
A great house at the top of the hill, shuttered for as long as anyone alive can remember. The shepherds drive their flocks around its wall in a wide curve and will not say why.

Inside, it is dry and clean and strangely empty of small living things. A windowless room in the cellar has a bar on the inside of its door and a bed made up for one who sleeps through the day. There is no name anywhere in the house.

the_hunger.title: The hunger
the_hunger.text:
It is not like appetite. It is a second pulse, patient and enormous, that rises as the night goes on and every time you use what you have become.

Animal blood quiets it, but only for a while. Human blood quiets it far better, and costs something that is harder to name. A starving creature does not choose, and the hunger, if it is left long enough, will choose for you.

the_sun.title: The sun
the_sun.text:
Every story says that the sun kills the dead. You have stood in it, and it has not killed you.

It does hurt. The light lies on you like a fever, and at midday you are weaker and the hunger runs hotter. But you are not ash, and you have no explanation for it. You have learned only that you should not tell anyone.

strix.title: Strix
strix.text:
In Roman folklore the strix is a night bird that feeds on the blood of sleepers, and the word is used for anything that drinks the living in the dark.

The men who came to Collesanto with torches used it of you, and they cried it like a hymn.

et_bloodlines.text:
A developer entry that shows how a bloodline is described once the hero has learned of it.

A second paragraph checks that long entries wrap and keep their spacing.

et_place.title: The Test Hill
et_place.text: A developer entry for a place. It unlocks the moment the sample chapter shows the hill.

et_lore.title: A Rule of Testing
et_lore.text: A developer entry in the Lore category. The sample chapter unlocks it only on one branch, so the codex shows both a found entry and an undiscovered one.

et_person.title: The Test Beloved
et_person.text: A developer entry that unlocks by itself when the hero meets the test beloved.

merchant_house.title: The Merchant line
merchant_house.text:
One of the five bloodlines that hold real power in the Senate of Blood. It does not rule by sword or by pulpit. It lends, and it keeps ledgers, and every throne in Rome owes it something.

Its houses hide in plain sight as warehouses, banks and shipping offices. A coven of the Merchant line is a family business with very old partners.

the_veil.title: The Veil
the_veil.text:
The first law of the dead: no human may know. Every other law grows from it. A witness is silenced or mistaken, and a hunter is a danger to everyone.

The Veil is not kept by fear alone. Most of the old ones keep it because they remember what the living do to what they cannot understand.

senate_of_blood.title: The Senate of Blood
senate_of_blood.text:
The Senatus Sanguinis mirrors the Senate of the living. Five bloodlines hold its real power. There were once six, and the sixth is not named.

It settles quarrels between covens, and it keeps the census of the made. It does not forgive a vampire who was never registered.

lictors.title: The Lictors
lictors.text: The Senate's enforcers take their name from the officers who walk before a Roman magistrate with rods bound in red cord. They are patient, they are old, and they are polite until the moment they are not.

collis.title: Collis
collis.text:
The name of the firm, from the Latin for a hill. It deals in oil, wine, ships and debts, and it is run in the daylight by a man the dead cannot match.

A firm leaves a paper trail, and a paper trail leads somewhere. Hide the link and the firm is safer and trusted less. Keep it and the name carries the hill with it.

the_lesser_cup.title: The lesser cup
the_lesser_cup.text: Animal blood will keep a vampire alive, and keep him close to what he was. It leaves him slower, hungrier and weaker in a fight, and some of the old ones say a little sad.\n\nThe made have gone over to it for as long as there have been the made. A great many of them have gone back. It is not a vow that anybody keeps once and is done with.

the_vigiles.title: The vigiles
the_vigiles.text: Rome's night watch, freedmen and slaves in cohorts, who carry buckets and hooks and put out the fires that a city of timber and thatch is forever starting. They are underpaid, underloved and the only people in Rome who walk its streets in the small hours with their eyes open.

the_igniferi.title: The Igniferi
the_igniferi.text: A sect devoted to Vesta, the goddess of the hearth, who hold that fire cleans what the dark has made. They wear grey, they carry a flame in a clay jar that is said never to go out, and they are very patient. They believe the strix, the night bird that drinks blood, is a thing to be burned out of Rome.

the_great_fire.title: The Great Fire
the_great_fire.text: It began in the shops about the Circus Maximus on the night of the full moon of Julius, and the wind from the river carried it up the Aventine and into the old quarters. It burned for the better part of a week, and by the end of it more than half the city lay in ashes.\n\nThe Senate of Blood had known the date for nine days. What the Senate said afterward was a good deal more careful than what it knew.

the_old_quarry.title: The old quarry
the_old_quarry.text: A hollow on the far side of the Esquiline where the first walls of Rome were cut, abandoned for four hundred years. The covens meet there when a matter is too large for any one house. At its far end a bronze door is set into the cliff, green with age, and the General's line keeps its back to it.

general_house.title: The General line
general_house.text: The line of brute strength and war, and the one the Senate uses when it needs a thing done. Its coven in Rome is led by Theron, who marched with Alexander. It answers to Tarrax, the Commander of the Lictors.

scribe_house.title: The Scribe line
scribe_house.text: The line of memory and secrets. Its keepers hold the records of the Senate, of the lines and of the dead, and they have long since noticed what the records leave out. Its coven in Rome meets in the Egyptian quarter under Meritamun.

the_bronze_door.title: The bronze door
the_bronze_door.text: A door of green bronze set into the cliff at the end of the old quarry. It has been knocked on from the inside for as long as anyone in the covens will admit to counting. Cedar bars cross it on the outside.

tarrax.title: Tarrax
tarrax.text: Commander of the Lictors and Firstborn of the General line. He keeps the Senate's peace with iron and does not speak of what is under the cliff.

the_general.title: The General
the_general.text: One of the Six, and the father of the General line. He lay beneath the hill until the door was opened. He asks for a drink, a year and a hat, in that order, and has not yet said what he wants.

surety.title: Surety
surety.text: The oldest custom of the dead. When one of them comes out of the dark, whoever first gives him drink, of their own blood or their own hand, becomes his surety. The Senate asks the ward no questions. It asks them of his surety.

the_watchers.title: The watchers of the Aventine
the_watchers.text: A handful of the vigiles who saw the city burn and saw, in the smoke, something that was not a fire. They have begun to meet in the evenings, in the station yard, with a wax tablet and a list. They do not mean to fight what they saw. They mean to see that somebody wrote it down.

the_keepers.title: The keepers of the hill
the_keepers.text: The oldest way for a human family to serve one of the dead: they hold the house, keep the shutters, know what lies below the stair, and hand the knowledge down. It is an oath that can last for centuries. It makes the family, for as long as it lasts, both a shield and a mark.

the_sack.title: Rome, 410
the_sack.text: Three summers of siege, a gate opened in the dark, and three days in which a very old city learned that it could be entered. It was not burned to the ground, and it was never again what it had been. The Senate of Blood left before the end of the week.

the_cistern_court.title: The court in the cistern
the_cistern_court.text: The Senate of Blood, as it sits at Constantinople: a forest of columns standing in black water, a platform of planks, and a great many old vampires who remember Rome and have agreed not to say so. The Emperor above them rules the day, and believes that he rules everything.

the_great_church.title: The Great Church
the_great_church.text: Justinian's church of the Holy Wisdom, finished in five years on the ashes of the one that burned in the riots. Its dome is lit from forty windows at its foot, so that it seems to hang by a chain from heaven. The court cannot go near it between dawn and dusk.

florence.title: Florence, 1474
florence.text: A republic of bankers under the shadow of a very great family, with a dome that nobody had thought could be built and a river that smells of tanning. It lends to kings, and it keeps the ledgers.

the_court.title: The Court of Florence
the_court.text: The vampires of the city sit as a court under a Prince, not a Senate. The Prince keeps the peace and the Merchant house keeps the purse, and neither says out loud which of the two is the more important.

san_custode.title: San Custode
san_custode.text: The guardian saint of the hill, who never ages, put out a fire at the mill and walked in the plague. He sleeps, they say, in a cellar under the shrine, and wakes when the hill is in danger. Nobody can say where the story began.

blood_licence.title: The licence of the Purse
blood_licence.text: Within the walls of Florence no vampire may feed on a citizen without a numbered brass licence from the Purse. It is one citizen a month, taken with consent or without harm, and the fee goes to the bank. The Prince keeps the peace and the Purse keeps the tally.

pazzi_medici.title: The Medici and the Pazzi
pazzi_medici.text: Two great banking houses and a quarrel that grows each year over alum, a will and a Pisan archbishopric. Some in the court find it useful to keep it warm.

priestess_line.title: The Priestess line
priestess_line.text: Old, proud and unhurried. Its princes hold courts rather than senates and rule by knowing what everyone owes.

the_purse.title: The bank of the Merchant house
the_purse.text: A plain door and a bronze ring, with a counting floor of forty tables, a licence office and a strong room under the street. It is one of the six great houses of Florence and has never been seen to fail.
